name: Olympiad Boss Arena - High-Order Multi-Step Battle
description: Culminating arena engine for complex multi-concept Grade 5 Olympiad Achievers section problems, integrating simultaneous logic, algebraic balance, spatial constraints, and multi-step deduction across the 5-stage mastery model.
author: TezMindz Olympiad Team

stages.name: Concept Discovery
stages.focus: Inspect integrated multi-constraint challenges, break complex questions into 2-3 manageable sub-goals

stages.name: Guided Simulation
stages.focus: Step-by-step boss counter-attacks, scaffolded multi-tier hints with sub-problem intermediate checks

stages.name: Rule Discovery
stages.focus: Formulate Olympiad heuristics: Work Backwards, Invariant Quantities, Pigeonhole Partition

stages.name: Controlled Practice
stages.focus: Dynamic high-order variations with randomised variables and changing battle conditions

stages.name: Anti-Memorisation Assessment
stages.focus: Unseen boss challenge with context inversion to verify conceptual mastery over rote tricks

sampleData.prompt: The Olympiad Dragon guards 3 chests. 2 Gold + 1 Silver = 190 kg. 1 Gold + 2 Silver = 170 kg. How heavy is one Gold chest?
sampleData.subPrompt: Combine both equations or isolate one chest type to pierce the Dragon's armor.
strategySteps: Step 1: Add both statements together: (2G + 1S) + (1G + 2S) = 3G + 3S = 360 kg.
Step 2: Divide by 3 to find (1 Gold + 1 Silver) = 360 ÷ 3 = 120 kg.
Step 3: Subtract (1G + 1S = 120 kg) from (2G + 1S = 190 kg) to isolate 1 Gold chest.
progressiveHints: Level 1 (Attention): Look at what happens if you combine everything on both scales: 3 Gold + 3 Silver chests.
Level 2 (Reasoning): 3 Gold + 3 Silver = 190 + 170 = 360 kg. Therefore, 1 Gold + 1 Silver = 360 ÷ 3 = 120 kg.
Level 3 (Demonstration): The first scale had (1 Gold + 1 Gold + 1 Silver) = 190 kg. Replace (1 Gold + 1 Silver) with 120 kg.
Level 4 (Full Solution): 1 Gold + 120 = 190 kg. So 1 Gold = 190 - 120 = 70 kg. The Gold chest weighs 70 kg.

ruleDiscovery.statementPrompt: Complete the Master Heuristic for Simultaneous Systems:
ruleOptions: Summing identical pairs of items allows finding the unit combination (1 of each) by division
Always guess and test random prime numbers until it matches
Multiply the two total weights together
ruleDiscovery.correctRule: Summing identical pairs of items allows finding the unit combination (1 of each) by division

sampleData.explanation: 3 Gold + 3 Silver = 360 kg => 1 Gold + 1 Silver = 120 kg. 1 Gold = (2G + 1S) - (1G + 1S) = 190 - 120 = 70 kg.
